paragraphs.title: The Closed Gate and Access to the Temple

easy.explanation: The passage describes the gate of the outward sanctuary that faced east, and it was shut.
easy.q: Which gate was shut at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: The Lord said, "It is for the prince; the prince, he shall sit in it to eat bread before the Lord."
easy.q: Who was permitted to sit in the gate and eat bread before the Lord?

easy.explanation: When Ezekiel saw the glory of the Lord, he fell upon his face.
easy.q: What did Ezekiel do when he saw the glory of the Lord fill the house?

answers: Because the people did not come
Because the Lord had entered through it
medium.explanation: The stated reason was that the Lord, the God of Israel, had entered through the gate.
medium.q: Why was the gate to remain shut?

answers: The ordinances, laws, and entrances of the house
medium.explanation: Ezekiel was told to mark well the ordinances, laws, entering in, and going forth of the sanctuary.
medium.q: What was Ezekiel commanded to pay careful attention to?

medium.explanation: In this context, a porch is a covered entrance or vestibule connected with the gate.
medium.q: What is a porch in the phrase "the way of the porch of that gate"?

answers: The prince had a special and defined access route
The gate was open to everyone
The prince could not enter the Temple
challenge.explanation: The passage gives the prince a particular route through the porch of the gate.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the prince entering and leaving by the same way?

answers: Entering the gate, offering a sacrifice, and leaving
Seeing God's glory, falling on his face, and receiving instructions
Eating bread, opening the gate, and keeping the Sabbath
challenge.explanation: Ezekiel sees the glory of the Lord, falls on his face, and then receives instructions concerning the Temple.
challenge.q: What is the central sequence of events in this passage?

answers: The gate remained shut, but the prince had access through the porch
The gate was open only to strangers
The prince entered only through the north gate
challenge.explanation: Although the gate itself remained shut, the prince was given access through its porch.
challenge.q: What distinguishes the closed gate from the prince's access?

paragraphs.title: Restrictions on Entry and the Roles of Levites and Priests

answers: A stranger uncircumcised in heart and flesh
easy.explanation: The Lord declared that no stranger uncircumcised in heart or flesh could enter the sanctuary.
easy.q: Who was not permitted to enter the sanctuary?

answers: They were to serve and keep charge at the gates
They were to enter the most holy place
easy.explanation: The Levites were assigned service, gatekeeping, and other duties concerning the house.
easy.q: What role was given to the Levites who had gone astray?

answers: The priests, the Levites, the sons of Zadok
easy.explanation: The sons of Zadok were allowed to come near, minister before the Lord, and offer the fat and blood.
easy.q: Who was permitted to come near the Lord for the central priestly service?

answers: Because they ministered before idols and caused Israel to fall
Because they did not eat bread
medium.explanation: They had ministered before idols and caused the house of Israel to fall into iniquity.
medium.q: Why did the Levites bear their iniquity and have their duties limited?

medium.explanation: Here, charge means responsibility for guarding or carrying out an assigned duty.
medium.q: What does "charge" mean in the phrase "having charge at the gates of the house"?

answers: The Levites served and guarded, while the sons of Zadok performed priestly service
The Levites offered sacrifices, while the sons of Zadok only guarded
medium.explanation: The Levites had service and guarding duties, while the sons of Zadok could approach the Lord and offer sacrifices.
medium.q: What was the main difference between the duties of the Levites and those of the sons of Zadok?

answers: Bringing them in polluted the house and was connected with breaking the covenant
Bringing them in strengthened the covenant
challenge.explanation: The strangers polluted the sanctuary, and the passage says that they had broken the Lord's covenant.
challenge.q: What connection is made between bringing strangers into the sanctuary and breaking the covenant?

answers: Faithfulness in keeping the sanctuary's charge is honored with priestly service
Only strangers may serve in holy things
Those who went astray receive the chief duty
challenge.explanation: The sons of Zadok kept the Lord's charge when Israel went astray, so they were allowed to minister near Him.
challenge.q: What principle is shown by the appointment of the sons of Zadok?

answers: Both are connected with serving and keeping the Lord's charge
Both sit in the eastern gate
Both eat every kind of offering
challenge.explanation: The Levites keep duties of service and guarding, while the sons of Zadok also keep the Lord's charge in their priestly work.
challenge.q: What duty is associated with both the Levites and the sons of Zadok?

paragraphs.title: Priestly Regulations in Service and Public Life

easy.explanation: The priests were to be clothed with linen garments, and wool was not to come upon them while they ministered.
easy.q: What material were the priests to wear when entering the gates of the inner court?

easy.explanation: The passage says that no priest was to drink wine when entering the inner court.
easy.q: What were the priests forbidden to drink when entering the inner court?

answers: The difference between the holy and profane, and between the unclean and clean
Only the names of the gates
easy.explanation: The priests were to teach the people to distinguish between the holy and profane and between the unclean and clean.
easy.q: What were the priests to teach the people?

answers: A maiden of Israel or a widow who had previously been married to a priest
medium.explanation: The priests could take maidens of the house of Israel or a widow who had had a priest before.
medium.q: What kind of woman could a priest take as his wife?

medium.explanation: They were to judge controversies according to God's judgments, keep His laws in assemblies, and hallow His Sabbaths.
medium.q: In what matters were the priests to judge and keep God's laws?

answers: His father, mother, son, daughter, brother, or unmarried sister
medium.explanation: The passage specifically names these close relatives, including a sister who had not had a husband.
medium.q: For which relatives could a priest defile himself by contact with the dead?

answers: Put off their service garments and put on other garments
challenge.explanation: When they went out to the people, they were to remove the garments in which they ministered and put on other garments.
challenge.q: What were the priests to do when they went from the inner court to the people?

answers: He had to reckon seven days
He had to enter the most holy place immediately
challenge.explanation: After being cleansed, he was required to reckon seven days.
challenge.q: What was required of a priest after he had been cleansed from defilement by the dead?

challenge.explanation: On the day he entered the sanctuary to minister, he was to offer his sin offering.
challenge.q: What was a priest to do on the day he entered the sanctuary to minister?

easy.explanation: The Lord said, "I am their inheritance" and "I am their possession."
easy.q: Who was the inheritance of the priests?

answers: Firstfruits, oblations, and the first of the dough
easy.explanation: The priests received firstfruits, offerings, and the first portion of the dough.
easy.q: What gifts were the people to give to the priests?

answers: Anything dead of itself or torn
easy.explanation: The priests were not to eat anything that had died of itself or had been torn, whether fowl or beast.
easy.q: What were the priests forbidden to eat?

answers: The meat offering, sin offering, and trespass offering
medium.explanation: The passage says they would eat the meat offering, the sin offering, and the trespass offering.
medium.q: Which offerings were the priests permitted to eat?

answers: The first portion of the dough
medium.explanation: The people were commanded to give the priest the first of their dough.
medium.q: What portion of the dough was to be given to the priest?

medium.explanation: The passage says that every dedicated thing in Israel would be theirs.
medium.q: What else would belong to the priests besides offerings and contributions?

answers: They would receive no land inheritance, because the Lord was their inheritance
They would receive the whole land
They would receive nothing from the people
challenge.explanation: The priests were denied a possession in Israel, while the Lord Himself was declared to be their inheritance.
challenge.q: What was the practical meaning of the statement that the priests would receive no possession in Israel?

answers: Giving the first of the dough to the priest was connected with causing blessing to rest in the house
The first of the dough was forbidden in the house
The dough was meant only for the Temple gates
challenge.explanation: The people were to give the first of their dough to the priest so that blessing might rest in the household.
challenge.q: What connection is made between the first of the dough and the household?

answers: They were animals that had died naturally or had been torn
They were gifts for the priests and sacrifices
They were kinds of priestly garments
challenge.explanation: The final verse forbids eating anything dead of itself or torn, whether it was a fowl or a beast.
challenge.q: How does the passage describe animals that the priests were forbidden to eat?
